subject: Marketplace ledger entity split & invoice routing notes
body:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datasight.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: finance@datasight.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Marketplace invoicing: multi-entity split and VAT handling

Hi Karthik and Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are close to toggling Redwood onto our marketplace procurement flow, but finance has a couple of practical asks before we can let purchases flow through AWS/GCP marketplaces: 

- Our corporate purchasing uses different entities for marketplace vs. direct SaaS (UK entity for marketplace). We need an explicit invoice split so marketplace charges route to the UK VAT entity and direct charges remain on the US legal entity.
- For the UK purchases, we require a VAT invoice (reverse-charge invoice format) and the supplier VAT number on the invoice.
- Due to internal policy we need either a signed W-9 for the US entity or a completed W-8BEN-E if Redwood prefers to invoice from a non-US entity for those lines.

Can you confirm what you support today and what routing metadata we need to provide on our end? If you can also attach: (a) your current W-9 and (b) an example marketplace invoice showing the VAT line, that would speed our procurement review.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement, DataSight
elena.ruiz@datasight.com

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datasight.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing: multi-entity split and VAT handling

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Invoice split & ledger mapping: We can produce marketplace-facing invoices that contain the VAT number and a reverse-charge line for EU purchases. Typical approach is: marketplace charges are invoiced by the Redwood UK entity (we route via the marketplace seller registration) while direct seat/subscription charges come from Redwood US. We will provide a CSV mapping of SKU -> invoice_entity for you to validate.

2) Tax forms: Attaching our signed W-9 for the Redwood US entity. If you require W-8BEN-E for an alternative invoicing flow, we can generate that but need legal coordinates.

3) Metadata/PO fields: To guarantee correct routing please provide the customer-side account id you use in the AWS Marketplace, and the billing entity P.O. number per purchase. We can also accept a HubSpot or procurement reference in the invoice metadata.

Attachments: W-9_Redwood_signed.pdf (attached), entity_invoice_mapping.csv (attached).

Action items
- Vanessa: can you take the lead with marketplace registration details and confirm the seller account currently registered for Redwood on AWS and GCP?
- Laura: loop in legal if they need to sign a reseller addendum (Elena mentioned a DocuSign later).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@datasight.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, AWS Marketplace Ops <aws-marketplace-partner@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing: multi-entity split and VAT handling

Hi Elena — copying AWS ops for visibility. Adding some implementation notes so procurement can plan.

- How we implement splits: We set the SKU-level seller entity in the marketplace listing metadata. At invoice time the marketplace will emit an invoice for the marketplace-registered seller (Redwood UK). We then separately emit a direct invoice for any components purchased off-marketplace. The key is consistent SKU mapping — I've attached a quick mapping file (entity_invoice_mapping.csv) to illustrate.
- VAT handling: For UK customers under reverse charge, invoices must include the customer VAT number and state "reverse charge applies". We can include Redwood UK VAT: GB999999999 in the invoice header. If DataSight prefers, we can also populate the "buyer VAT" field on the marketplace order metadata so the marketplace invoice includes it automatically.
- W-9 vs W-8: If you want the US entity to be the invoicer for marketplace lines (uncommon), we will need a W-8BEN-E on file showing the non-US recipient status; otherwise the marketplace seller flow from the UK entity is simplest (no US tax withholding).

AWS note (from AWS Marketplace Ops): "Ensure the seller registration lists the UK VAT entity and that tax IDs are populated in Seller Central. Marketplace invoices rely on the seller metadata — if those fields are empty marketplace invoices will omit VAT lines and create downstream reconciliation work."

I'll draft a short checklist for procurement:
- Confirm buyer VAT number and entity names
- Provide marketplace customer account ID (AWS/GCP)
- Confirm PO format and where PO will live (HubSpot reference or PO number to appear on invoice)
- Sign reseller addendum if DataSight requires specific indemnities

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Channel Partnerships, Redwood
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment: entity_invoice_mapping.csv (1 KB)

Thanks Karthik and Vanessa — this is helpful.

We will:
- Share our UK VAT number and the AWS account ID by EOD.
- Confirm PO format (we use PO-DS-#####). Please place the PO number in the invoice metadata.
- We have reviewed the W-9 you attached — acceptable. We will request a DocuSign reseller addendum to our legal team; can Redwood legal sign electronically?

Two quick asks before procurement closes:
1) Can you provide a sample marketplace invoice (PDF) that shows the VAT reverse charge line and Redwood UK VAT number?
2) Can you confirm whether the marketplace invoice will include the buyer VAT number if we populate that in the order metadata?

If you can send both items I will fast-track approval and loop our AP for purchase order issuance.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Procurement, DataSight
